 Japan's Nikkei falls over 1% as chip stocks slide ahead of Nvidia earnings
 SECTIONS Japan's Nikkei falls over 1% as chip stocks slide ahead of Nvidia earnings By Anupam Nagar , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 10:02:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Japan’s Nikkei fell 1.6% on Monday, dragged down by heavyweight semiconductor stocks amid caution ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s anticipated IPO. Advantest and Tokyo Electron led losses, while financial stocks and retailers outperformed. Investors remained wary of AI valuations and Nvidia’s leadership uncertainty, despite broader market resilience.
 ETMarkets.com Investors are closely monitoring Nvidia's earnings announcement on Tuesday for clues about the strength of demand for AI-related investments.
 Japan's Nikkei share average fell sharply on Monday, weighed down by heavyweight chip stocks as investors turned cautious ahead of Nvidia's quarterly earnings on Tuesday and the highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic later this week, according to a report by Reuters.
 The Nikkei 225 declined 1.6% to 60,182.50 at the midday break. In contrast, the broader Topix index fell a relatively modest 0.4%.

Nvidia suppliers and chip equipment makers led the losses, with Advantest tumbling 9.9% and Tokyo Electron declining 5.2%. The two stocks together accounted for 904 points of the Nikkei's total 960-point decline, according to the report.
 Also Read | Global Market Today: Asian stocks subdued as US futures gain; Nvidia earnings, Fed minutes in focus 
The weakness came amid growing concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence-driven market rally. Investors are closely monitoring Nvidia's earnings announcement on Tuesday for clues about the strength of demand for AI-related investments.
 Live Events
Another major test of investor sentiment will be Anthropic's IPO. The creator of the Claude chatbot is expected to price its much-anticipated public offering on Wednesday, followed by its stock market debut on Thursday.
 The report stated that caution around AI-related stocks was building despite the absence of fresh negative developments over the weekend.
 Also Read | Anthropic's record IPO faces some big questions 
The selling pressure was concentrated in AI-linked sectors, which were among the worst performers across the Tokyo Stock Exchange's 33 industry groupings. The nonferrous metals sector, which includes data centre cable makers Furukawa Electric and Fujikura, dropped 5.8%, while the electrical appliances sector, which includes Advantest, declined 3%.
However, the broader market showed some resilience, with gainers outnumbering losers on the Nikkei. As many as 115 of the index's 225 constituents advanced, compared with 108 decliners, while two stocks remained unchanged.
Financial stocks and retailers outperformed. Credit card company Credit Saison surged nearly 17% to emerge as the Nikkei's biggest gainer after raising its earnings forecast. Furniture retailer Nitori climbed 7.8% following its financial results.
The retail sector was the best performer among the Tokyo Stock Exchange's industry groups, rising 2.6%, according to Reuters.
The nervousness around AI stocks also comes amid uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership. Reuters reported that media accounts of developments involving CEO Jensen Huang have fuelled speculation about the chipmaker's leadership, with reports also suggesting that Nvidia had approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas for the role.
